name: South Korea

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (resident taxed worldwide)
paths.note: Foreign dividends go into global income at up to 45% plus 4.5% local tax (49.5%) with credit for foreign withholding; gains on foreign shares are taxed at 20% plus 2% local (22%). No wealth tax. Inheritance tax is estate-based at 10% to 50% after a KRW 500 million lump-sum deduction, on the worldwide estate of a resident.

paths.name: Family investment company (Korean stock company)
paths.note: The parents' company holds the portfolio and pays corporate income tax (22% at the margin with local tax) on dividends and gains; payout to the parents is taxed at 43.45% (dividend gross-up and credit). The shares are in the estate (unlisted shares at net asset value; the 20% controlling-shareholder valuation premium may apply, see open questions). A family trust is tax-transparent and a public-interest foundation is not a family vehicle, so no path for either.

checks.working: All foreign: KRW 1,000,000,000 of dividends with 15% foreign withholding (KRW 150,000,000) and KRW 500,000,000 of gains on foreign shares. Top rates assumed: each spouse's global income already fills the lower bands, so the dividends are taxed at the top bracket, 45% above KRW 1 billion (Income Tax Act art. 55; PwC table), on financial income above KRW 20 million that is added to global income (arts. 14(3), 17(1)(vi)); in reality the first KRW 1 billion of a person's income would be taxed at lower bands. National tax 45% x 1,000,000,000 = 450,000,000, less the foreign tax credit of 150,000,000 (art. 57; within the limit, which is the income tax multiplied by foreign income over total income and far above 15%) = 300,000,000. Local income tax is 10% of the national scale, 4.5% x 1,000,000,000 = 45,000,000 (Local Tax Act art. 92); the foreign tax is within the national limit, so it does not reduce it. Dividends 345,000,000. Gains on foreign shares: 20% national + 10% of that as local tax = 22% (Income Tax Act arts. 94(1)(iii)(c), 104; NTS overseas stocks guide) x 500,000,000 = 110,000,000; the KRW 2.5 million basic deduction is ignored. Total 455,000,000. The 10% gross-up and dividend credit apply only to Korean dividends. Health-insurance contributions on financial income are not taxes and are left out. Local Tax Special Measures Act (local credits) was not opened.

Company with taxable income of KRW 1,500,000,000 (dividends 1,000,000,000 from foreign portfolio shares with 15% withholding, gains 500,000,000), fiscal year from 1 January 2026; payout tax excluded; no running costs are recorded in the tax file. Corporate income tax: 10% x 200,000,000 + 20% x 1,300,000,000 = 20,000,000 + 260,000,000 = 280,000,000 (Corporation Tax Act art. 55; PwC; EY). Foreign tax credit of 150,000,000 (15% of the dividends), within the limit of tax x foreign income / total income (280,000,000 or at least 186,666,667), leaves 130,000,000 (art. 57; PwC). Local income tax: the base is the taxable income less the foreign tax credited, 1,500,000,000 - 150,000,000 = 1,350,000,000 (Local Tax Act art. 103-19(2)); rates 1% to 200,000,000 and 2% above (art. 103-20; PwC) = 2,000,000 + 23,000,000 = 25,000,000. No exclusion applies to foreign portfolio dividends below a 10% stake (PwC). Total 130,000,000 + 25,000,000 = 155,000,000. The minimum tax applies after special-law reductions only and is not triggered. The 20% additional tax on retained earnings applies to conglomerate companies only (PwC).
checks.model_note: The engine applies one flat rate of 22% to all income and subtracts the 15% withholding: 0.22 x 1,500,000,000 - 150,000,000 = 180,000,000. By law the first KRW 200 million bears 10% national and 1% local tax, 22,000,000 less, and the local base is reduced by the foreign tax credited, 2% x 150,000,000 = 3,000,000 less; the engine has no rate bands and no local-base reduction (compare the Dutch BV and German GmbH notes).

checks.working: Lump-sum deduction KRW 500M (art. 21; above the basic 200M + 3 x 50M). Financial-asset deduction: listed shares are financial assets, 20% capped at KRW 200M (art. 22). Taxable estate 10,000M - 500M - 200M = 9,300M. Scale (art. 26): 9,300M x 50% - 460M = 4,190M. Filing credit 3% (art. 69) = 125.7M. Tax 4,064.3M.
checks.model_note: The engine has no 3% filing credit (art. 69 Inheritance and Gift Tax Act) and no financial-asset deduction (art. 22: 20% of net financial assets, capped at KRW 200M), so it computes 4,290M on the 9.5bn base.

assumptions: Top rates are assumed for personal income: dividends are taxed at the 45% bracket plus 4.5% local tax (49.5%), as if the couple's other taxable income fills the lower bands; in reality the first KRW 1 billion of each person's income is taxed at lower bands. The KRW 2.5 million basic deduction on share gains and health-insurance contributions are ignored.
Foreign dividends carry 15% withholding, creditable in full against the national income tax (the local tax is not reduced).

The 5-year path assumes the foreign dividends and the proceeds of foreign share sales stay abroad and nothing is paid in Korea; the family does not qualify unless it has a residence status (the F-2/F-5 investor schemes were not verified).
The company is funded at today's value; selling existing foreign shares to it would be a taxable disposal for the individual.
At the first death (year 30) the estate passes to the spouse under the spouse deduction; the checks are for the second death with three adult children and the KRW 500 million lump-sum deduction.
The 10-year aggregation of lifetime gifts and the gift-tax deductions are not modelled.

The 5-of-10-year foreign resident rule is left out: foreign-source income is taxed when paid in or remitted to Korea (Income Tax Act art. 3(1) proviso), and the family spends EUR 400,000 a year there, so most of it would be taxed; the engine cannot separate remitted capital from income. Same treatment as Ireland's remittance basis.

left_out.note: A foreign national who has lived in Korea 5 years or less in the last 10 pays tax on foreign income only when it is paid in Korea or sent there (Income Tax Act art. 3(1)). With EUR 400,000 a year spent in Korea, much of the foreign income would be sent there, and the projection cannot tell capital sent in from income; the rule ends after 5 years.

open_questions: Needs an engine change: valuation of the family company's unlisted shares for inheritance tax: net asset value, plus a 20% premium for a controlling shareholder's shares unless the company is an SME or mid-sized company (Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act art. 63(3)). Whether a family investment company qualifies as an SME was not established; if not, the taxable value is 1.2 times the portfolio, which the engine cannot express. No inheritance check is given for the company path for this reason.

Needs an engine change: the 3% credit for filing on time (art. 69) and the financial-asset deduction (art. 22, up to KRW 200 million, if a foreign-custody portfolio counts) are not in the tax file; the 3% credit is in the check's model_difference.

The tax file's 5-year regime now codes foreign-share gains and foreign real estate at 0% on the remittance basis (statute art. 3(1) proviso, read in the Act text mirror; foreign real estate per PwC); the Enforcement Decree was not opened.

The Local Tax Special Measures Act (local dividend and foreign tax credits) was not opened: local tax is taken as 10% of the national scale, reduced by the dividend credit but not by the foreign tax credit within the national limit, as in the tax file.
The local corporate income tax rates (1%/2%/2.2%/2.5%) and the dividend exclusion percentages (30% below 20%) are from PwC; the Corporation Tax Act text was not available.
The tax file records no running cost for the family company; the check counts none.
Needs an engine change: remittance basis (spending in the country deemed to come from foreign income first) would let the special regime be projected honestly.
